title: Per-invocation econ UX journey and wires
content:
Quick context / TL;DR:
- Goal: surface per-invocation (tokenized) cost + latency signal in ways teams can action: debug regressions, compare model variants, and configure routing/policy fallbacks.
- Difference from previous token dashboards: center the interaction around the invocation (request) as the primary entity, not an abstract token-summary. We show token breakdowns as expandable detail.

High-level user problems we want to solve:
- Engineering: why is path X showing 3-4x cost? (need to correlate model version, prompt length, batching config, quantization).
- Product/PM: prove we can reduce unit cost by changing cache thresholds / model route mixes.
- SRE/Support: detect degradation (latency P95 jump) and map to model change / rollout.

Assumptions and constraints:
- We have token-level counts from runtime + per-route cost metrics (estimated $/tok) available via telemetry.
- Prefix caching/KV reuse data is spotty for older releases; design must gracefully show "no cache data" state.
- We must avoid exposing raw $ in some regulated accounts; show relative delta or internal-only toggle.

Primary metrics to display (invocation-level):
- Invocation start time (localTZ)
- Model & model variant
- Total tokens (input/expansion/output)
- Estimated cost (invocation USD) and cost breakdown by stage (prompt, generation, tools)
- Latency percentiles (p50,p95,p99) for tokens and total time
- Batching indicator (was this batched? batch size)
- KV cache hit ratio / reused tokens count
- Hardware profile (gpu type, quantization)

Personas and flows:
1) Debugger (ML infra engineer)
- Filter: route=/chat/complete, model=rwkv-x, p95>500ms last 10m
- Inspect top slow invocations, open an invocation detail panel, expand token timeline, see high-latency tokens and associated kernel traces (link to infra logs)

2) Cost owner (product owner)
- Run cohort: all invocations for feature flag beta in last 7 days
- Compare average cost/invocation across model variants and note impact of prefix caching. Export CSV for finance.

3) SRE (incident)
- Alert: p95 increased 2x after a deploy; use the dashboard to quickly find correlated model variant rollouts and fallback events.

Wireframe variants (sketch descriptions) - tried to keep named patterns short:
A. Invocation list + flyout (compact)
- Left: filter bar + list of invocations (each row: timestamp, route, model, cost est, latency p95)
- Right: flyout when you click an invocation. Shows timeline (tokens on x-axis), stacked bars: CPU/GPU time per token, cached tokens shaded, cost attribution badges.
- Pros: quick triage, simple.
- Cons: limited space, timeline small for long outputs.

B. Invocation canvas (canvas-first)
- Large central canvas: invocation timeline with zoom. Top lane = tokens; middle lanes = subsystem timings (kernel, IO, batching wait); bottom lane = cost by token. Side panel with metadata and actions (open logs, pin, create ticket).
- Pros: great for deep-dive and correlation.
- Cons: heavier, slower to load for lists.

C. Aggregate cohort view + peek details
- Top: cohort selectors (route, model, timeframe). Middle: heatmap of cost vs latency buckets; clicking a cell shows sample invocations. Bottom: table of model variant deltas and suggested actions (e.g., decrease max_tokens, enable prefix cache).
- Pros: decision-centric for PMs.
- Cons: less helpful for single-invocation debugging.

D. Tiny-mode: sparkline row view for dashboards
- Rows show sparkline for cost per invocation and latency overlay; hover opens micro-widget with token waterfall. Good for large lists and at-a-glance monitoring.

Micro interactions / UX details:
- Token timeline hover: show token text (if allowed by account policy) + token-level time and cost. If policy prohibits, show token hash + size.
- Expandable cost breakdown: prompt vs generation vs tools. For tool calls, link back to tool logs.
- Anonymize toggle: switch between internal (exact $/tokens) and external view (percent delta, normalized units).
- Save "investigation snapshots" (pin an invocation + notes) that can be shared with support. Stored as short link.

Backlog / grooming notes (rough prioritization):
- P0: Invocation list + flyout w/ basic token counts, cost estimate, p95. (JIRA-INV-412)
- P0: Backend API endpoints for per-invocation token timeline and cache metadata (ENG-serve-998).
- P1: Canvas zoom + kernel timing lanes (UX research to decide lane granularity).
- P1: Aggregate cohort heatmap + suggested actions (prototype A/B test).
- P2: Anonymize toggle + account policy gating (privacy/legal review).
- P2: Export CSV / finance-ready report generator.
- P3: Attachments: auto-suggested remediation (e.g., re-route to cheaper variant if cost > threshold).

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we show full token text by default in invite-only accounts? (privacy)
- Should cost be shown as absolute USD by default or percent delta vs baseline? (sales/legal ask for hidden $)
- What's the backend SLA for fetching detailed token timelines for a list of 50 invocations? We need a perf budget.
- Do we provide a way to replay an invocation (re-run with same model/config) from the UI? Aligns with solutions engineering ask.

Data and performance considerations (notes for infra):
- Token timeline payload can be large. Design API to support streaming of token detail and a lightweight summary for list views.
- Cache metadata must include: cache type (prefix/kv), hits, reused_tokens_count. For missing data, we show "unknown" and an action to request deeper trace.
- Backend should compute cost attribution server-side to avoid shipping pricing logic to client. But show breakdown structure so UI can render.

Accessibility / small-screen behavior:
- On phone, default to compact list + single-pane detail; hide token-by-token view behind "deep dive" link to conserve bandwidth.
- Ensure color choices in heatmap meet contrast and colorblind-safe palettes.

Experiment ideas (A/B):
- A: show USD in top-left vs B: show normalized "cost units" + link to translate to USD. Measure support tickets about exposed $ and finance downloads.
- A: show suggested action cards (e.g., "enable prefix cache") vs B: show only raw metrics. Measure action rate and false positives.

Sketches to produce (next week):
- Compact flyout with token small-tiles (8 variants) + copy for no-cache state. (owner: Elias)
- Canvas deep-dive with lane toggles and export button (owner: Marta)
- Cohort heatmap prototype with suggested actions panel (owner: Jonas)

Meeting notes (2025-02-21 sync):
- PMs asked for CSV export priority elevated for finance review — moved to P1 if rapid CSV is feasible.
- Legal flagged token text exposure; Aditi to draft policy gating flows by 2025-02-28.
- Infra confirmed token timeline streaming feasible but needs a caching tier; estimate 3 sprints.

Next steps / immediate todo:
- Produce 3 low-fi wireframes (compact flyout, canvas, cohort) before UX review (due 2025-02-28).
- Spike: infra to prototype token timeline streaming endpoint and return perf numbers (ENG spike owner: Elias).
- Create JIRA epic and decompose P0 tasks (Aditi).

Notes to self (scribbles):
- Keep invocation the anchor: makes support and ownership simpler.
- Think about integrating with Rollouts page: highlight when a rollout caused cost/latency drift.
- Add a "what changed" diff view between two invocations (show model, config, cache differences).

Edge-case examples stored here for reference (short):
- Invocation with 0 output tokens but high cost = likely tool call charged separately.
- Invocation long tail: first 100 tokens low-latency then P95 spikes at tokens 450-460 = possible kernel swap / GPU memory pressure.
- Invocation with negative cache reuse (computed incorrectly) = watch for telemetry bugs.

Endnotes:
- This doc is intentionally rough. Use it as a base for next UX grooming session. Capture sketches in /drive images under the same folder and link them into the ticket.
- I'll convert to a polished PRD if stakeholders align on P0 scope by next week.
